name: Pluto
hook: The demoted planet Jeopardy refuses to forget — discovery, moons and the 2006 demotion.

facts.label: its 1930 discovery
facts.statement: Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto in 1930 at Lowell Observatory, completing the search Percival Lowell had begun.

facts.label: a dwarf planet
facts.statement: In 2006 Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet, joining Ceres and Eris, and it is smaller than Mercury.

facts.label: Charon
facts.statement: Charon, Pluto's largest moon, was discovered in 1978, is just over half Pluto's diameter, and is named for the ferryman of the dead.

facts.label: Styx
facts.statement: Pluto's moons carry underworld names — Charon, Nix, Hydra, Kerberos and Styx, the most recently discovered.

facts.label: the Kuiper Belt
facts.statement: Pluto is one of the larger Kuiper Belt objects, the icy belt beyond Neptune where Eris was discovered in 2005.

facts.label: New Horizons
facts.statement: NASA's New Horizons probe revealed nitrogen-ice glaciers on Pluto and the heart-shaped region now called Tombaugh Regio.

facts.label: its eccentric orbit
facts.statement: Pluto's orbit is so eccentric that for 20 years of every 248 it comes closer to the Sun than Neptune does.
